messages:
alina: quick update from the kernel census for the block-packing experiments on GQA vs MQA + paged-kv layouts. ran sweep across block sizes [64,128,256], packing thresholds, and two seqlen buckets (<=64, >64).

matt: nice, any large regressions?

alina: overall median token latency improved for <=64 with 128-block packing on GQA (about -9% p50), but for >64 sequences the same packing yields +12% due to cache straddle.

jordan: can you paste the raw numbers? micro-bench output is helpful.

alina: sure, pasted below (local xA100, single model fp16, 32 batch):
```
seqlen_bucket,layout,block_sz,p50_ms,p95_ms,notes
<=64,gqa,64,12.4,23.1,ok
<=64,gqa,128,11.3,21.5,winning
<=64,mqa,128,11.8,22.0,small win
>64,gqa,128,28.6,54.2,cache straddle +KV page thrash
>64,gqa,256,25.1,48.0,better alignment
>64,mqa,256,24.8,46.5,good for multiq
```

sasha: looks like the drop for >64 at 128 is the cause. may be because per-shard KV stripe crosses page boundary with that packing. can you attach the cache-miss heatmap?

alina: attaching inline sample (summarized):
- 128 block: 34% miss on first stripe, 12% on subsequent
- 256 block: 8% miss uniformly

matt: is the kernel selector currently aware of per-request seqlen distribution? we could gate 128-block path only for <=64 requests.

jordan: in 2.1.4 we added a simple seqlen flag but autotune disabled for MQA. commit 7a3f1b9 toggles it, might explain some diffs.

sasha: proposal: make kernel-picker use a tiny census vector: {p(<=64), p(<=128), avg_seqlen} sampled every minute. choose packing that minimizes expected token-latency (cost model from bench).

alina: prototype implemented. small tradeoff: sampling and recompute every 60s adds ~0.6% CPU overhead on the scheduler thread.

perf-bot: bench-run complete: https://ci.internal/bench/2934567890 - delta table posted, CI artifacts archived.

ci-bot: build 2934f7 passed: kernels + autotune smoke ✅

matt: next steps: 1) try gating 128-block packing to seqlen<=64 via runtime flag, 2) rebench mixed workloads (p95 matters), 3) add fallback to 256-block if KV-page-miss>20% in last sample.

alina: I'll push a small PR with runtime flag + policy algo. leaving notes in the PR about memory fragmentation risk for 256 pack.

jordan: also snapshot a trace for a failing request (txn id 0x9f4c). helps repro.

sasha: +1, and add a short eval set with synthetic multiq workloads to the autotuner so it doesn't bias purely on <=64.

alina: cool. logging action items in the ticket: https://redwood/issue/INF-6721. will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
